name: gradient-background
title: GradientBackground
purpose: Render a deterministic, slowly animated procedural field behind application content without requiring image or video input.
useFor: Reproducible generated artwork exported from Background Studio
avoidFor: Dense content without a protective surface

composition.renderer: One Three.js WebGLRenderer, orthographic camera, full-screen plane, and Balsa-owned single-pass ShaderMaterial.
composition.configuration: Versioned schema-two BalsaBackgroundConfig with automatic schema-one migration, preset defaults, configuration overrides, and direct prop overrides in that order.
composition.noiseSeparation: Structural field octaves and frequency shape waves independently from visible noise amount, octaves, and frequency; fine grain remains a separate final texture treatment.
composition.seedSafety: The renderer maps full-range configuration seeds into a small deterministic shader-safe range before hashing so floating-point precision cannot collapse procedural noise.
composition.studioSimulations: Background Studio compares structurally distinct Storefront, Dashboard, and Editorial shells; every simulated label, metric, byline, and content string is explicit placeholder or lorem-ipsum copy rather than plausible live content.
composition.studioHandoff: Background Studio groups project export into Balsa CLI, Manual, and Prompt disclosures; CLI is initially expanded, encodes the exact current configuration into one shell-safe background create --config command with no intermediate download, and shows the generated Vue import/template usage; Prompt explicitly obtains GradientBackground through the public add command; PNG capture remains separate.

accessibility: The canvas is decorative, aria-hidden, non-interactive, and pointer-transparent.
Reduced-motion users receive one static rendered frame.
Forced-colors users receive a system-color fallback.
No meaning or control state depends on background motion.
commonMistakes: Placing readable content directly over high-contrast forms without a surface.
Running several full-viewport instances when one shared background is enough.
Coupling the primitive to an application palette or theme store.
Using more than six or fewer than two color stops.
